label: JZ Mock B · Paper 2 · Question 14
knowledgePattern: Sum scaled trigonometric solutions as a convergent geometric series
solution:
Put t=2kx. The stated interval becomes 0≤t≤2π, and sint=1/2 gives t=π/6 or 5π/6. Thus x=π/(6·2k) or 5π/(6·2k), and F(k)=π/2k.

The series starts at k = 1, with first term π/2 and common ratio 1/2. It converges because the ratio has magnitude below one, and its sum is (π/2)/(1−1/2)=π. Answer C.

hints.title: Name the whole angle
hints.body: Put t=2kx. Multiply both ends of the allowed x-interval by 2k too.
hints.recap: The same angle equation may then appear for every k.
hints.pitfall: The multiplier is 2 to the power k, not 2k.
hints.pause: Solve the equation in t on its complete interval.

recall.reminder: Transform the interval with the trigonometric input.

hints.title: Add the roots for one k
hints.body: Convert the permitted t-values back to x, and add them to get F(k). Then write F(1), F(2) and F(3).
hints.recap: The first few values show how the sum changes with k.
hints.pitfall: F(k) is the sum of the roots, not the number of roots.
hints.pause: Find the common ratio and calculate the infinite sum.

recall.reminder: An infinite GP uses its actual first term and a ratio with magnitude below 1.
